COMPANY: 86,651+12,958-85,203=14,406; 14,406-62,259=-47,853 = reported PBT exactly. Both ties are exact, confirming no column-swap/dual-rendering artifact in this filing (unlike some prior CSE filings in this project) -- the Group and Company P&L columns, segmental note, and SOCE all agree. finance_costs stores the filing's own NET finance cost figure (net of finance income, since no gross split is disclosed on this page); finance_income is left blank rather than guessed. trade_receivables and trade_payables use the filing's combined 'Trade and Other Receivables' / 'Trade & Other Payables' lines (no separate trade-only breakout given). eps_diluted set equal to eps_basic since the filing presents a single EPS line with no dilutive instruments disclosed. capex includes both 'Purchase & Construction of PP&E' and 'Investment in immature plantations' (both are capital investment in productive assets for a plantation company).

interim_updates.note_text: Kotagala Plantations PLC (KPPLC) swung from a Group profit of Rs.47.9mn in Q1 FY2025/26 to a Group loss of Rs.49.3mn in Q1 FY2026/27, a Rs.97.2mn deterioration, on revenue that fell 27.6% YoY to Rs.1,028.6mn. All three plantation segments weakened: Tea gross profit fell to Rs.105.2mn from Rs.127.3mn (-17.4%) as higher tea prices and per-kg profitability were more than offset by a drop in quantity sold (management attributes this to 'geopolitical impact' on stock holding) and a 15% government-mandated wage increase; Oil Palm gross profit fell to Rs.58.1mn from Rs.84.6mn (-31.3%) on a 12% crop decline; Rubber's gross loss was roughly flat at Rs.76.6mn versus Rs.76.4mn (Group) a year earlier. Group gross profit overall fell 36.0% to Rs.86.7mn. Total net finance cost improved to Rs.62.3mn from Rs.84.1mn (-25.9%), a partial offset, aided by the successful rescheduling of the company's entire Rs.500mn debenture balance to a 5-year term at a reduced 7.5% interest rate (from a higher prior rate) with a defined monthly repayment plan. Other/sundry income collapsed 84.0% YoY, from Rs.80.9mn to Rs.13.0mn -- this single swing (Rs.67.9mn) is larger than the entire net loss and is the single largest driver of the year-on-year deterioration, but the filing gives no note detail on what made up the prior year's Rs.80.9mn other income figure, so its composition (e.g. one-off disposal gain, insurance claim, etc.) cannot be confirmed from this document alone.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for KOTA -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Additionally, this filing's Statement of Financial Position presents only 30.06.2026 vs 31.03.2026 (FYE) columns, with no 30.06.2025 prior-year-same-quarter balance sheet, so a balance-sheet YoY comparison is not possible from this document; only income-statement YoY is available (shown above).
interim_updates.takeaway: The headline swing to a Rs.49.3mn Group loss overstates how much worse underlying plantation operations got: gross profit fell a real but more moderate 36% on lower volumes and higher wages across Tea, Rubber and Oil Palm, while an unexplained 84% drop in other/sundry income (Rs.80.9mn to Rs.13.0mn, composition undisclosed) did most of the work in pushing the bottom line from profit to loss.
operational_highlights: Group revenue fell 27.6% YoY to Rs.1,028.6mn; Group loss of Rs.49.3mn vs a Rs.47.9mn profit in Q1 FY2025/26.
Tea segment gross profit Rs.105.2mn vs Rs.127.3mn (-17.4%), despite higher tea prices, on lower quantity sold and a 15% wage hike.
Oil Palm segment gross profit Rs.58.1mn vs Rs.84.6mn (-31.3%) on a 12% decline in crop.
Rubber segment gross loss broadly flat at Rs.76.6mn (Group) vs Rs.76.4mn a year earlier.
Total net finance cost improved 25.9% to Rs.62.3mn (Rs.84.1mn prior) after the entire Rs.500mn debenture balance was rescheduled over 5 years at a reduced 7.5% rate.
Net assets per share fell to Rs.8.12 (Company) from Rs.8.23 as at 31 March 2026.
key_drivers: Other/sundry income: Rs.80.9mn (Q1 FY2025/26) to Rs.13.0mn (Q1 FY2026/27), a Rs.67.9mn (-84.0%) swing -- the single largest driver of the YoY profit deterioration; composition not disclosed in this filing.
Oil Palm segment: gross profit -31.3% on a 12% crop volume decline -- the weakest-performing segment this quarter.
Government-mandated 15% wage increase (industry-wide) raised cost per kg across Tea, Rubber and Oil Palm, offsetting higher tea prices.
Debenture rescheduling (Rs.500mn, 5-year term, 7.5% rate) reduced finance costs and partially cushioned the operating decline.
